advances: A witness for a relaxed screen with actual endpoint cuts and equal endpoint cap areas. It does not have compatible three-fiber geometry or a bad raw budget.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The coordinate change preserves area. The first cut is $\xi=0$, one quarter of the way from the apex to the base, so its chord is $H/4$. The missed similar triangle has area fraction $1/16$. The total area is $H(4e/3)/2$.

The level $x_2=-1$ on the second cut has signed margin $\eta+3/2-\xi/2$. At the lower base vertex it is $-(H+e-3)/2<0$, at the upper base vertex $(H-e+3)/2>0$, and at the apex $3/2+e/6>0$. Linear interpolation gives a missed corner triangle with area fraction
$$
\frac{(H+e-3)^2}{2H(H+4e/3)}.
$$
Indeed the two edge fractions from the lower vertex to the cut are $(H+e-3)/(2H)$ and $(H+e-3)/(H+4e/3)$. The horizontal span of the cut is $(4e/3)$ times the latter fraction; it is the normalized section length on this line. Reflection in $\eta=0$ exchanges the second and third cuts, preserves area and the horizontal span, and this span is also the normalized length on the diagonal third line. For the stated rationals, $132750^2=375000\cdot375948/8$, so the missed fraction equals $1/16$. Substitution gives the three lengths and the area stated.

The middle quantities follow by clipping the triangle with vertices $(-1,-1),(2,-1),(-1,2)$. Since the middle centers are zero and the three computed $a_i$ are positive and less than $2$, the chord bounds hold. The first full reciprocal weight is $(1+a_2)/(3+a_2+2a_1)$, with difference $2/9-p_1=7652051/228752541>0$. For $B=T$ each endpoint $B$ cut at level $1$ is a null facet, so each actual cap on the three separate fibers has mass $Q$. But the midpoint of the apex of $A$ and $(-2,1)\in B$ has first coordinate $-121599/80987<-1$ and is not in $K$. Finally, $|K|=|B|=9/2$ gives the stated strict budget difference.
statement: Use $T=\{x:x_1\le1,\ x_2\le1,\ x_1+x_2\ge-1\}$, $K=-T$, and $v_i=(1,0),(0,1),(-1,-1)$. In the determinant-one coordinates $\xi=x_1+1$, $\eta=x_2+x_1/2$, let $A$ have apex $(-e/3,0)$ and base endpoints $(e,\pm H/2)$, with $H=375000/80987$ and $e=711/80987$. Each cut $v_i\cdot x=-1$ is proper. All three captured areas equal $15a/16$ with $a=|A|=177750000/6558894169$, and the normalized chord lengths are $a_1=93750/80987$ and $a_2=a_3=19750/4778233$. The three bisected middle chords have lengths $k_i=2$ and areas $q_i=2$ in the corresponding upper caps at level zero, so the cap ratios are $4/9<128/279$ and the sorted middle profile is tight. The inequalities $a_i\le k_i$ and $|c_i|\le a_i(k_i-a_i)/(k_i+2a_i)$ hold. Yet the full reciprocal weights from $k_i+2a_i$ have $p_1=4797983/25416949<2/9$. With $B=T$, the menu budgets all equal $Q=2+15a/16$ but $(A+B)/2\not\subseteq K$ and $Q-(2/9)(a+|K|+|B|)=103a/144>0$.
title: Equal actual endpoint cap areas do not repair the relaxed inverse-weight screen
